definition_zh: 出席；照料；处理
definition_en: to be present at an event, or to take care of someone or something
core_image: 服务员侧身站在桌边，等你开口
scene: 会议室里坐满了人。Two hundred people attended the meeting.
sceneCN: 这里 attend 是「出席」（第 1 个义项：到场参加）；句意是两百人出席了会议。

senses.title: Be present at
senses.definition: to be present at an event, school or meeting
senses.definitionCN: 到场参加活动、课程或会议
senses.example: Two hundred people attended the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 两百人出席了会议。
senses.why: Attend comes from Latin attendere, 'to stretch the mind toward', so presence began as directing one's attention to a place and then came to mean being there.
senses.whyCN: attend 源自拉丁语 attendere「把心思伸向」，所以「到场」最初是把注意力投向某处，后来才指人真的在那里。

senses.title: Take care of
senses.definition: to deal with or care for someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人，或着手处理某事
senses.example: A nurse attended to the injured man.
senses.exampleCN: 一名护士照料那位受伤的男子。
senses.why: The same stretching of mind toward a person becomes nursing, and toward a problem becomes dealing with it, which is why attend takes the preposition to here.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「把心力伸向」用在人身上就是照看，用在事情上就是着手处理，因此这个义项要接介词 to。

intro.en: Attend is a word about stretching the mind toward something.
intro.cn: attend 是一个把心思伸向某物的词。

items.en: tendere meant 'to stretch'.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」。

items.en: attendere meant 'to stretch the mind toward'.
items.cn: attendere 意为「把心思伸向」。

items.en: atendre meant 'to wait for or expect'.
items.cn: atendre 意为「等待、期待」。

items.en: English attend covered waiting on and being present.
items.cn: 英语 attend 兼指侍候与到场。

items.en: Attendance at events became the leading sense.
items.cn: 「出席活动」成为主要义项。

note.en: The look-alike group is the tend family; the near-meaning group gives verbs of presence and care.
note.cn: 形近组是 tend 词族；近义组是表示到场与照料的动词。

normalIntro.en: Attend first meant to lean your mind toward, then to show up in person.
normalIntro.cn: attend 先指把心思倾过去，后指人亲自到场。

normal.en: For events, attend takes a direct object: attend a meeting.
normal.cn: 指参加活动时直接带宾语：出席会议。

normal.en: For care or problems, use attend to.
normal.cn: 指照料或处理时用 attend to。

normal.en: The double t comes from ad- plus tendere.
normal.cn: 双 t 来自 ad- 与 tendere 的结合。

normal.en: The noun is attendance, not attend.
normal.cn: 名词是 attendance。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TEND.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a whole row of chairs filled before the speaker begins.
abstract.cn: 想象演讲开始前整排椅子都坐满。

abstract.en: See a nurse turning toward a call bell.
abstract.cn: 想象护士转身走向呼叫铃。

abstract.en: See a head leaning slightly toward a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象脑袋微微倾向说话的声音。

examples.en: Two hundred people attended the meeting.
examples.cn: 两百人出席了会议。

examples.en: A nurse attended to the injured man.
examples.cn: 一名护士照料那位受伤的男子。

examples.en: She attends a language class twice a week.
examples.cn: 她每周上两次语言课。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tend（伸）：把心思伸向某处，是人到场；把心力伸向某人，是照看；伸向问题，是处理。

root: 源自拉丁语 attendere「把心思伸向」，由 ad-「向」与 tendere「伸」构成，经古法语 atendre 进入英语；由专注、侍候引申为到场出席。

sensesIntro.en: Presence, care and handling are three ways of stretching toward something.
sensesIntro.cn: 到场、照看与处理，是同一个「伸向」的三种落点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mind leaning toward a point.
core.cn: 核心意象：心思向一个点倾过去。

intro.en: The tend root, 'to stretch', also gives extend, intend and tension.
intro.cn: 词根 tend 意为「伸」，也构成 extend、intend 与 tension。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere is the base, and its compounds fill English with reaching words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 是词基，其复合词让英语充满「伸展」类的词。

items.meaning: to stretch the mind to a plan
to lean or take care of

definition_zh: 注意；注意力；照料
definition_en: the act of focusing the mind on something, or practical care
core_image: 整间屋子的目光都落在同一处
scene: 老师敲了敲桌子。The class gave the teacher their full attention.
sceneCN: 这里 attention 是「注意力」（第 1 个义项：心思集中到某处）；句意是全班把注意力完全集中在老师身上。

senses.title: Focus of the mind
senses.definition: the act of directing your mind toward something
senses.definitionCN: 把心思集中到某件事上
senses.example: The class gave the teacher their full attention.
senses.exampleCN: 全班把注意力完全集中在老师身上。
senses.why: Attention is attend plus -tion, so the stretching of the mind toward a thing becomes the focus itself, something a speaker can ask a room to give.
senses.whyCN: attention 是 attend 加 -tion，把「心思伸向某处」变成那份专注本身，所以老师可以要求全班把它交出来。

senses.title: Practical care
senses.definition: care or treatment given to a person or problem
senses.definitionCN: 给予某人或某问题的照护与处置
senses.example: The patient needs immediate medical attention.
senses.exampleCN: 这名病人需要立即接受医疗照护。
senses.why: When the mind leans toward someone in need, the focus turns into hands-on care, which is why hospitals speak of medical attention.
senses.whyCN: 当心思倾向有需要的人时，专注就变成了实际动手的照护，所以医院会说医疗照护。

intro.en: Attention is the noun of stretching the mind, formed on the verb attend.
intro.cn: attention 是把心思伸出去的名词，由动词 attend 构成。

items.en: tendere meant 'to stretch'.
items.cn: tendere 意为「伸展」。

items.en: attendere meant 'to stretch the mind toward'.
items.cn: attendere 意为「把心思伸向」。

items.en: attentio meant 'a stretching toward'.
items.cn: attentio 意为「向某处的伸展」。

items.en: English attention named heed and care.
items.cn: 英语 attention 指留心与照看。

items.en: Psychology made attention a central term.
items.cn: 心理学使 attention 成为核心术语。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the attent stem; the near-meaning group names focus and care.
note.cn: 形近组共享 attent 词干；近义组是表示专注与照料的词。

entries.definition: to be present or care for

normalIntro.en: Attention is a stretch of the mind that can also become a helping hand.
normalIntro.cn: attention 是心思的一次伸展，也可以变成伸出的援手。

normal.en: It is uncountable in the focusing sense: pay attention.
normal.cn: 表示专注时不可数：pay attention。

normal.en: The verb after the phrase is pay, not give, in the fixed idiom.
normal.cn: 固定说法是 pay attention，不说 give attention。

normal.en: Medical attention means treatment, not concern.
normal.cn: medical attention 指治疗，不是关心。

normal.en: The adjective is attentive, the adverb attentively.
normal.cn: 形容词是 attentive，副词是 attentively。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TEN-tion.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See every face in a room turned the same way.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子人脸都朝同一个方向。

abstract.en: See a spotlight narrowed to one chair.
abstract.cn: 想象聚光灯收窄到一把椅子上。

abstract.en: See a hand already reaching for a first-aid box.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手已经伸向急救箱。

examples.en: The class gave the teacher their full attention.
examples.cn: 全班把注意力完全集中在老师身上。

examples.en: The patient needs immediate medical attention.
examples.cn: 这名病人需要立即接受医疗照护。

examples.en: A loud noise drew everyone's attention.
examples.cn: 一声巨响吸引了所有人的注意。

dict_mnemonic.text: attend（把心思伸向）加 -tion：心思伸出去，是注意力；心思落到需要的人身上，是照护。

root: 由 attend 加 -tion 构成；attend 源自拉丁语 attendere「把心思伸向」，因此 attention 既指专注，也指落到某人身上的实际照护。

sensesIntro.en: Attention can be a beam of focus or a hand of care.
sensesIntro.cn: attention 可以是一束专注的光，也可以是一只照护的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every eye turned to one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：所有目光转向同一点。

intro.en: The -tion ending turns the verb of stretching into the state of being focused.
intro.cn: 结尾 -tion 把表示伸展的动词变成专注的状态。

latinIntro.en: Latin attendere and attentio supply the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 attendere 与 attentio 提供了整族词。

definition_zh: 态度；看法；姿势
definition_en: a way of thinking or feeling about something, or a bodily posture
core_image: 身体微微前倾，把立场写在姿态上
scene: 面试官问他对加班怎么看。His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
sceneCN: 这里 attitude 是「态度」（第 1 个义项：对事情的看法与姿态）；句意是他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。

senses.title: Way of thinking
senses.definition: a settled way of thinking or feeling about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事较为固定的想法与感受
senses.example: His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。
senses.why: Attitude came from Italian attitudine, 'aptness or posture', from Latin aptitudo 'fitness', so the mental sense grew out of a body set a certain way.
senses.whyCN: attitude 来自意大利语 attitudine「适宜、姿态」，其拉丁词源 aptitudo 意为「适合」，所以心里的看法是从身体的摆法长出来的。

senses.title: Bodily posture
senses.definition: a position in which the body is held
senses.definitionCN: 身体摆出的姿势
senses.example: He stood in an attitude of prayer.
senses.exampleCN: 他摆出祈祷的姿势站着。
senses.why: The oldest sense was the body's pose, and this concrete use survives in literary description even though the mental sense now dominates.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思是身体的摆法，尽管如今心里的看法占主流，这个具体义仍保留在文学描写中。

intro.en: Attitude is a word of fitness that began with the body and moved into the mind.
intro.cn: attitude 本是个表示「适合」的词，从身体移到了心里。

items.en: aptus meant 'fit or suited'.
items.cn: aptus 意为「适合的」。

items.en: aptitudo meant 'fitness or posture'.
items.cn: aptitudo 意为「适合、姿态」。

items.en: attitudine meant 'a pose of the body'.
items.cn: attitudine 意为「身体的姿势」。

items.en: French attitude kept the painter's sense of a pose.
items.cn: 法语 attitude 保留画家所说的姿态义。

items.en: The mental sense of a view became dominant.
items.cn: 表示看法的心理义成为主流。

note.en: The look-alike group is easily confused in spelling; the near-meaning group names views and poses.
note.cn: 形近组拼写易混；近义组是表示看法与姿态的词。

entries.definition: a public position on an issue
the way the body is held

normalIntro.en: Attitude began as the body's pose and became the mind's pose.
normalIntro.cn: attitude 从身体的姿势变成心里的姿势。

normal.en: Use attitude to or towards for the object of a view.
normal.cn: 表示看法对象时用 attitude to 或 towards。

normal.en: The plural attitudes is common in surveys.
normal.cn: 调查中常用复数 attitudes。

normal.en: Strike an attitude means pose, often for effect.
normal.cn: strike an attitude 指摆姿势，常带做作意味。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with aptitude, which is ability.
normal.cn: 不要与 aptitude 混淆，后者是天资。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AT-ti-tude.
normal.cn: 重音在第一音节。

abstract.en: See shoulders squared before a difficult question.
abstract.cn: 想象难题来临前肩膀一挺。

abstract.en: See a model frozen in a painted pose.
abstract.cn: 想象模特定格在一个画中的姿势。

abstract.en: See a face that has already decided before the words come.
abstract.cn: 想象话还没出口，脸上的判断已经定了。

examples.en: His relaxed attitude surprised the interviewer.
examples.cn: 他轻松的态度让面试官感到意外。

examples.en: He stood in an attitude of prayer.
examples.cn: 他摆出祈祷的姿势站着。

examples.en: Public attitudes towards the plan have changed.
examples.cn: 公众对这项计划的态度已经改变。

dict_mnemonic.text: attitude 与 aptitude 同源，本义是「摆得合适的样子」：身体的摆法是姿势，心里的摆法是态度。

root: 源自拉丁语 aptitudo「适合、姿态」，经意大利语 attitudine 与法语进入英语；本指身体的姿势，后引申为心里对事物的固定看法。

sensesIntro.en: A pose of the body and a pose of the mind are the same word.
sensesIntro.cn: 身体的摆法与心里的摆法，是同一个词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body set at a slight angle.
core.cn: 核心意象：身体摆出一个微斜的角度。

intro.en: The -itude ending marks a noun of state, as in aptitude and solitude.
intro.cn: 结尾 -itude 表示状态名词，如 aptitude 与 solitude。

latinIntro.en: Latin aptus, 'fit', also gives apt and aptitude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aptus「适合」也是 apt 与 aptitude 的来源。

definition_zh: 律师；代理人
definition_en: a lawyer, or a person given legal power to act for another
core_image: 一个人被正式授权，替另一个人开口
scene: 法庭上被告身边坐着一位穿黑衣的人。Her attorney spoke for her in court.
sceneCN: 这里 attorney 是「律师」（第 1 个义项：受委托代理法律事务的人）；句意是她的律师在法庭上替她发言。

senses.title: Lawyer
senses.definition: a lawyer who is qualified to act for people in legal matters
senses.definitionCN: 有资格在法律事务中代表他人的律师
senses.example: Her attorney spoke for her in court.
senses.exampleCN: 她的律师在法庭上替她发言。
senses.why: Attorney comes from Old French atorner, 'to assign', so the attorney was first the one assigned to stand in another's place, and law kept that role as the courtroom lawyer.
senses.whyCN: attorney 来自古法语 atorner「指派」，本指被指派代替他人的人，法律沿用了这个角色，用它指法庭上的律师。

senses.title: Authorized agent
senses.definition: a person given legal power to act for someone else
senses.definitionCN: 获得法律授权、代替他人行事的人
senses.example: She acted as attorney for her elderly father.
senses.exampleCN: 她作为年迈父亲的代理人行事。
senses.why: The original sense of a person appointed to act in another's place survives in documents such as a power of attorney, where no courtroom is involved.
senses.whyCN: 「被指派代替他人行事」这个本义保留在授权书一类的文件里，那种场合与法庭无关。

intro.en: Attorney is a French word of appointment, and appointment still lies at its centre.
intro.cn: attorney 是法语中表示「指派」的词，指派至今仍是它的核心。

items.en: atorner meant 'to assign or arrange'.
items.cn: atorner 意为「指派、安排」。

items.en: atorne meant 'one appointed'.
items.cn: atorne 指「被指派的人」。

items.en: English attorney named a legal representative.
items.cn: 英语 attorney 指法律上的代表人。

items.en: Attorney at law became the courtroom lawyer.
items.cn: attorney at law 成为出庭律师的称呼。

items.en: Attorney became the ordinary word for lawyer.
items.cn: 在美国英语中，attorney 成为律师的常用说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the attorney stem; the near-meaning group names legal professionals.
note.cn: 形近组共享 attorney 词干；近义组是法律职业的称呼。

entries.definition: a legal adviser in a case

normalIntro.en: An attorney is someone appointed to speak in your place.
normalIntro.cn: attorney 是被指派到你位置上说话的人。

normal.en: The plural is attorneys, not attornies.
normal.cn: 复数是 attorneys。

normal.en: In the United States, attorney is the everyday word for lawyer.
normal.cn: 在美国英语里 attorney 就是日常说的律师。

normal.en: Power of attorney names the document, not the person.
normal.cn: power of attorney 指授权书，不指人。

normal.en: The word has a soft c sound in the middle? No, it has no c.
normal.cn: 词中并没有 c，注意不要按拼写误读。

normal.en: Stress the second syllable: at-TOR-ney.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节。

abstract.en: See a black robe standing at a courtroom table.
abstract.cn: 想象法庭桌边站着一位黑袍人。

abstract.en: See a signed paper granting someone a voice.
abstract.cn: 想象一份签字文件把发言权交给别人。

abstract.en: See two chairs, one empty and one occupied by a representative.
abstract.cn: 想象两把椅子，一把空着，一把坐着代理人。

examples.en: Her attorney spoke for her in court.
examples.cn: 她的律师在法庭上替她发言。

examples.en: She acted as attorney for her elderly father.
examples.cn: 她作为年迈父亲的代理人行事。

examples.en: The company hired an attorney to review the contract.
examples.cn: 公司聘请了一名律师审阅合同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 古法语 atorner 是「指派」：被指派到你的位置上说话的人，是律师；被授权替你处理事务的人，是代理人。

root: 源自古法语 atorner「指派、安排」，指被指派代替他人行事的人；进入英语后专指法律代表，在美国英语中成为律师的常用称呼。

sensesIntro.en: Courtroom advocate and authorized agent are two settings for one appointed role.
sensesIntro.cn: 法庭上的辩护人与授权代理人，是同一个被指派角色的两种场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a seat occupied on another's behalf.
core.cn: 核心意象：替别人坐上的那个位置。

intro.en: Attorney is a borrowed whole word, but it anchors a small legal family.
intro.cn: attorney 是整体借入的词，但撑起了一个小型法律词族。

latinIntro.en: The French stem atorner goes back to Latin ordinaire, 'to arrange'.
latinIntro.cn: 法语词干 atorner 可追溯到拉丁语 ordinaire「安排」。

definition_zh: 吸引；引起（注意、兴趣）；招致（批评、麻烦）
definition_en: to pull someone or something toward a place, or to make people interested or notice something
core_image: 一块磁石把四周的铁屑都拉成一个小圈
scene: 夜市摊主把灯调亮，路过的人不由自主地靠近。The bright stall attracted a crowd within minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 attract 是「吸引」（第 1 个义项：把人或物拉向自己）；句意是明亮的摊位几分钟内就吸引了一群人。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：有吸引力的；好看的

senses.title: Draw near
senses.definition: to pull someone or something toward a place or person
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物拉向某处或某人
senses.example: The flowers attract bees in early summer.
senses.exampleCN: 初夏时这些花吸引蜜蜂。
senses.why: The Latin base trahere means 'to draw or pull', so the first sense is a physical pull, as a magnet draws iron.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 trahere 意为「拉、拖」，所以第一义项是物理意义上的拉近，像磁石把铁吸过来。

senses.title: Arouse interest
senses.definition: to make people interested in something or make them notice it
senses.definitionCN: 使人对某事物产生兴趣或注意到它
senses.example: The title attracted my attention at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这个标题立刻引起了我的注意。
senses.why: The pull moves from the body to the mind: eyes and curiosity are drawn toward the thing, though nothing physically moves.
senses.whyCN: 这种「拉」从身体转到心里：目光和好奇心被牵过去，物体本身并没有移动。

senses.title: Bring something bad
senses.definition: to cause something unpleasant to come to you
senses.definitionCN: 招来不愉快的事，如批评或麻烦
senses.example: His remarks attracted sharp criticism.
senses.exampleCN: 他的言论招致尖锐的批评。
senses.why: Here the pull works in reverse: your own words or deeds draw consequences onto you, and those consequences are usually unwelcome.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「拉」方向相反：自己的言行把后果拉到自己身上，而这类后果通常不受欢迎。

intro.en: Attract is built from a Latin verb meaning to draw something toward oneself.
intro.cn: attract 由拉丁语中表示「把东西拉向自己」的动词构成。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw, pull or drag'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、拖、牵引」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus trahere made attrahere, 'to draw to oneself'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 trahere 构成 attrahere，意为「拉向自己」。

items.en: The past participle attractus described something already drawn near.
items.cn: 过去分词 attractus 描述已被拉近的东西。

items.en: English attracten first meant to draw or allure.
items.cn: 中古英语 attracten 最初表示拉近或引诱。

items.en: The word widened to interest, appeal and unwanted consequences.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到引起兴趣、产生吸引力以及招致不良后果。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root tract; the near-meaning group gives other verbs of drawing people in.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁词根 tract；近义组是其他表示「把人拉过来」的动词。

entries.definition: to draw together and become smaller
to pull or pull in interest

normalIntro.en: Attract is a pull, first on things, then on eyes and minds.
normalIntro.cn: attract 是一种拉力，先拉物体，再拉目光和心思。

normal.en: The prefix at- is really ad-, meaning to.
normal.cn: 前缀 at- 其实是 ad-，意为「向」。

normal.en: Picture a magnet: whatever it draws is attracted.
normal.cn: 想象一块磁石：被它拉过来的东西就是被吸引的。

normal.en: Attract attention and attract interest are the two everyday patterns.
normal.cn: attract attention 与 attract interest 是两个最常用的搭配。

normal.en: Attract criticism shows the same pull applied to bad results.
normal.cn: attract criticism 说明同一个「拉」也能用在糟糕的结果上。

normal.en: The noun is attraction and the adjective is attractive.
normal.cn: 名词是 attraction，形容词是 attractive。

abstract.en: See iron filings jump and cling to a magnet.
abstract.cn: 想象铁屑跳起来，紧紧贴在磁石上。

abstract.en: See moths circling a bright window at night.
abstract.cn: 想象夜里飞蛾绕着一扇亮着的窗打转。

abstract.en: See a spotlight swing across a stage and stop on one singer.
abstract.cn: 想象一束追光扫过舞台，停在一个歌手身上。

examples.en: The bright stall attracted a crowd within minutes.
examples.cn: 明亮的摊位几分钟内就吸引了一群人。

examples.en: The flowers attract bees in early summer.
examples.cn: 初夏时这些花吸引蜜蜂。

examples.en: Bright colours attract young children.
examples.cn: 鲜艳的颜色会吸引小孩子。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tract（拉）：把人和目光往自己这边拉，就是吸引；拉来的若是批评和麻烦，就是招致。

root: 源自拉丁语 attrahere，由 ad-「向」与 trahere「拉」构成，过去分词 attractus；经中古英语 attracten 进入英语，由「拉近」引申为引起兴趣，再引申为招致后果。

sensesIntro.en: A magnet, a headline and a careless remark all pull something toward them.
sensesIntro.cn: 磁石、标题和一句失言，都在把东西往自己这边拉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a magnet drawing iron filings into a tight ring.
core.cn: 核心意象：磁石把铁屑拉成一个紧贴的小圈。

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', links attract with distract and extract.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，把 attract 与 distract、extract 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere, 'to draw', also gives tractor and traction.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere「拉」也是 tractor 与 traction 的来源。

definition_zh: 吸引力；吸引人的事物（景点）；引力
definition_en: the power of something to interest or please people, a place or thing that draws visitors, or a force that pulls objects together
core_image: 游乐园里最高的那座塔，人群都朝它走过去
scene: 导游在车上指着窗外一片灯火，告诉大家下一个看点。The old castle is the town's main attraction.
sceneCN: 这里 attraction 是「吸引人的地方、景点」（第 2 个义项）；句意是这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。

senses.title: Pulling power
senses.definition: the quality that makes people feel interested or drawn to something
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生兴趣、被牵过去的那种性质
senses.example: The attraction of country life is its peace.
senses.exampleCN: 乡村生活的吸引力在于它的宁静。
senses.why: The noun names the force itself rather than the thing exerting it, so it can describe an abstract quality like peace or freedom.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指的是「力」本身，而不是发出这股力的东西，所以可以形容宁静、自由这类抽象特质。

senses.title: Place worth visiting
senses.definition: a place or thing that people visit because it is interesting
senses.definitionCN: 因为有趣而吸引人去参观的地方或事物
senses.example: The castle is the town's main attraction.
senses.exampleCN: 这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。
senses.why: The abstract pull is turned into a countable object: whatever does the pulling can be counted as one attraction among many.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的「拉力」被具体化成可数的东西：凡是发出吸引力的，都能算作众多景点中的一个。

senses.title: Force between objects
senses.definition: a force that makes objects move toward each other
senses.definitionCN: 使物体相互靠近的力
senses.example: Gravity is the force of attraction between masses.
senses.exampleCN: 重力是物体之间相互吸引的力。
senses.why: Physics kept the oldest and most literal part of the word: bodies really do pull one another, with no interest or feeling involved.
senses.whyCN: 物理学保留了这个词最古老、最字面的部分：物体确实在互相拉，其中没有兴趣或情感。

intro.en: Attraction turns the act of drawing into a thing: the pull itself.
intro.cn: attraction 把「拉」这个动作变成一样东西：那股拉力本身。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、牵引」。

items.en: attrahere meant 'to draw toward'.
items.cn: attrahere 意为「拉向」。

items.en: attractio named the action of drawing something near.
items.cn: attractio 指「把东西拉近」这一动作。

items.en: French attraction carried the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语 attraction 把这个名词带进英语。

items.en: English added tourist sights and the force studied in physics.
items.cn: 英语又加上了旅游景点与物理学研究的作用力两层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tract root; the near-meaning group gives words for charm and appeal.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tract 词根；近义组是表示魅力与吸引的说法。

entries.definition: the act of drawing something out
a person or thing that attracts

normalIntro.en: Attraction is either the pull or the thing that pulls.
normalIntro.cn: attraction 要么指那股拉力，要么指发出拉力的东西。

normal.en: The ending -tion marks a noun built on the verb attract.
normal.cn: 词尾 -tion 表明这是由动词 attract 构成的名词。

normal.en: Tourist attraction is the phrase you will meet most often in travel texts.
normal.cn: 旅游文本里最常见的是 tourist attraction 这个搭配。

normal.en: Attraction to someone names a feeling of being drawn.
normal.cn: attraction to someone 表示被某人吸引的那种感觉。

normal.en: In physics, attraction is the opposite of repulsion.
normal.cn: 在物理学里，attraction 与 repulsion 相对。

normal.en: The verb is attract and the adjective is attractive.
normal.cn: 动词是 attract，形容词是 attractive。

abstract.en: See a lit fairground tower visible from every street.
abstract.cn: 想象一座亮着的游乐塔，从每条街都看得见。

abstract.en: See a crowd flowing like water toward one gate.
abstract.cn: 想象人群像水一样朝同一个门口流去。

abstract.en: See two magnets click together across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象两块磁石隔着桌子啪地吸到一起。

examples.en: The attraction of country life is its peace.
examples.cn: 乡村生活的吸引力在于它的宁静。

examples.en: The castle is the town's main attraction.
examples.cn: 这座古堡是镇上最主要的景点。

examples.en: Gravity is the force of attraction between masses.
examples.cn: 重力是物体之间相互吸引的力。

dict_mnemonic.text: attract 加 -ion 变成名词：那股把人拉过去的力量是吸引力，被拉过去看的地方就是景点。

root: 源自拉丁语 attractio，来自 attrahere「拉向」，词基 trahere 意为「拉」；经法语 attraction 进入英语，由「拉近的动作」引申为吸引力，再具体化为景点，并在物理学中指物体间的引力。

sensesIntro.en: One word covers the pull, the place that pulls, and the force between two bodies.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既指拉力，也指发出拉力的地方，还指两个物体之间的作用力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd streaming toward one lit tower.
core.cn: 核心意象：人群朝一座亮着的塔涌过去。

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', runs through the whole attraction family.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，贯穿 attraction 整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere also produced traction and tractor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 还产生了 traction 与 tractor。

items.meaning: the pull or the thing that pulls

definition_zh: 好看的；有魅力的；有吸引力的（条件、提议）
definition_en: pleasant to look at, or good enough to make people want it
core_image: 橱窗里的一件东西让人走过又退回来多看一眼
scene: 中介带人看房，一进门就被落地窗外的景色吸引。The flat is small but very attractive.
sceneCN: 这里 attractive 是「好看的、有魅力的」（第 1 个义项）；句意是这套公寓不大，但非常讨人喜欢。

pos.zh: 形容词：好看的；有吸引力的

senses.title: Pleasing to look at
senses.definition: pleasant in appearance, so that people enjoy looking at you or it
senses.definitionCN: 外表讨人喜欢，让人愿意多看
senses.example: She wore a simple but attractive dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一条简单却很好看的连衣裙。
senses.why: The word describes the effect on the viewer: something attractive draws the eye before any judgment is made about it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词描述的是看的人受到的影响：有魅力的东西先抓住目光，人才会去评判它。

senses.title: Worth accepting
senses.definition: good enough to make people want to accept it or join in
senses.definitionCN: 条件足够好，让人愿意接受或参与
senses.example: They made us an attractive offer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给了我们一个很有吸引力的报价。
senses.why: The pull is no longer visual but practical: a price, a job or a deal can attract a person just as a face can.
senses.whyCN: 这里的吸引力不再是视觉上的，而是实际利益上的：价格、工作或交易也像面容一样能把人拉过来。

intro.en: Attractive simply means having the power to draw.
intro.cn: attractive 的意思就是「具有拉过来的力量」。

items.en: trahere meant 'to draw or pull'.
items.cn: trahere 意为「拉、牵引」。

items.en: attractus was the participle 'drawn toward'.
items.cn: attractus 是表示「被拉近」的分词。

items.en: attractivus described something with power to draw.
items.cn: attractivus 描述「具有吸引力」的东西。

items.en: French attractif carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 attractif 把这个形容词带进英语。

items.en: English widened it from physical pull to beauty and good deals.
items.cn: 英语把它从物理拉力扩展到美貌与划算的条件。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that sound close; the near-meaning group holds words of beauty and appeal.
note.cn: 形近组是读音相近的词；近义组是表示美貌与吸引力的词。

normalIntro.en: Anything that draws people can be called attractive, from a face to a salary.
normalIntro.cn: 凡是能把人吸引过来的，从面容到薪水，都可以叫 attractive。

normal.en: The ending -ive makes it an adjective describing what does the attracting.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ive 使它成为形容词，描述发出吸引力的那一方。

normal.en: Use attractive to before the person or group being drawn.
normal.cn: 用 attractive to 引出被吸引的人或群体。

normal.en: An attractive offer is about terms, not looks.
normal.cn: attractive offer 说的是条件，不是长相。

normal.en: The noun is attraction and the verb is attract.
normal.cn: 名词是 attraction，动词是 attract。

normal.en: Do not mix it up with attentive, which means watching closely.
normal.cn: 不要与 attentive 混淆，后者意为专心留意。

abstract.en: See a shop window that stops people in the middle of a step.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇橱窗让人走到一半就停下来。

abstract.en: See a price tag that makes a buyer smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一个价签让买家笑起来。

abstract.en: See a face turn a whole room without a word.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸一句话不说就让整个房间转过头来。

examples.en: The flat is small but very attractive.
examples.cn: 这套公寓不大，但非常讨人喜欢。

examples.en: She wore a simple but attractive dress.
examples.cn: 她穿了一条简单却很好看的连衣裙。

examples.en: They made us an attractive offer.
examples.cn: 他们给了我们一个很有吸引力的报价。

dict_mnemonic.text: attract 加 -ive：会把人拉过来的，就是有吸引力的；拉眼睛的是好看，拉钱包的是条件划算。

root: 源自拉丁语 attractivus「有吸引力的」，来自 attrahere「拉向」，词基 trahere 意为「拉」；经法语 attractif 进入英语，由物理拉力扩展到外貌与条件的吸引力。

sensesIntro.en: A beautiful face and a generous salary pull people in the same grammatical way.
sensesIntro.cn: 一张好看的脸和一份优厚的薪水，在语法上是以同一种方式把人拉过去的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shop window that makes a walker turn back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇橱窗让路人回头。

intro.en: The root tract, 'to draw', is the same one heard in attract and distraction.
intro.cn: 词根 tract 意为「拉」，在 attract 与 distraction 里听到的是同一个词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin trahere also gives tractor, traction and extract.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 trahere 还给出 tractor、traction 与 extract。

definition_zh: 属性，特质；把……归因于；认为（作品）出自……
definition_en: a quality that belongs to a person or thing, or to say that something is caused by or made by someone
core_image: 一件物品上系着标签，写着它是什么、从哪里来
scene: 老师在评语里写下这个学生最突出的特点。Patience is the attribute every good teacher needs.
sceneCN: 这里 attribute 是「特质、属性」（第 1 个义项）；句意是耐心是每位好老师都需要的特质。

pos.zh: 动词：把……归因于；认为出自

senses.title: Mark of a thing
senses.definition: a quality or feature that belongs to a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 属于某人或某物的性质或特征
senses.example: Kindness was his most striking attribute.
senses.exampleCN: 善良是他最突出的特质。
senses.why: The noun keeps the old sense of something allotted to a thing: an attribute is a quality assigned to whatever carries it.
senses.whyCN: 名词保留了「分派给某物」的旧义：属性就是分配给承载者的那种性质。

senses.title: Name the cause
senses.definition: to say that something is the result of a particular cause
senses.definitionCN: 认为某结果是某个原因造成的
senses.example: She attributes her success to hard work.
senses.exampleCN: 她把自己的成功归功于努力。
senses.why: The verb reverses the direction: instead of giving a quality to a thing, you give an effect back to the cause that produced it.
senses.whyCN: 动词把方向倒过来：不是把性质给某物，而是把一个结果送回造成它的原因。

senses.title: Name the maker
senses.definition: to believe that a work was produced by a particular person
senses.definitionCN: 认为某件作品是由某个特定的人创作的
senses.example: The painting was attributed to an unknown artist.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画被认定出自一位不知名的画家之手。
senses.why: Authorship is treated as another kind of allotment: the work is assigned back to the hand that made it.
senses.whyCN: 作者身份被视为另一种「分派」：把作品重新分配给做出它的那只手。

intro.en: Attribute began as a legal word for something allotted to a person.
intro.cn: attribute 最初是个法律用语，指分派给某人的东西。

items.en: tribuere meant 'to allot or assign'.
items.cn: tribuere 意为「分配、分派」。

items.en: ad- 'to' plus tribuere made attribuere, 'to assign to'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 tribuere 构成 attribuere，意为「分派给」。

items.en: attributum was the thing assigned or credited.
items.cn: attributum 指被分派或归到某人名下的东西。

items.en: French attribut named a quality belonging to something.
items.cn: 法语 attribut 指属于某物的性质。

items.en: English split the word into a noun of quality and a verb of assigning causes.
items.cn: 英语把它分成表示性质的名词与表示归因的动词。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tribute root; the near-meaning group gives nouns of quality and verbs of explaining causes.
note.cn: 形近组共享 tribute 词根；近义组是表示性质的名词与解释原因的动词。

a feature of a person or thing

normalIntro.en: As a noun it names a quality; as a verb it hands an effect back to its cause.
normalIntro.cn: 作名词时它指一种性质；作动词时它把结果交还给原因。

normal.en: The noun stresses the first syllable, the verb the second.
normal.cn: 作名词时重音在第一音节，作动词时重音在第二音节。

normal.en: Attribute to is the verb pattern: attribute success to luck.
normal.cn: 动词搭配是 attribute to，例如把成功归因于运气。

normal.en: An attribute is something a person or thing simply has.
normal.cn: attribute 作名词时，就是人或物本身具有的某种特质。

normal.en: To attribute a painting to an artist is to name its maker.
normal.cn: 把画作归到某位画家名下，就是认定它的作者。

normal.en: The root tribute means to give or allot.
normal.cn: 词根 tribute 意为「给予、分配」。

abstract.en: See a label tied to an object, naming what it is.
abstract.cn: 想象一张标签系在物品上，写明它是什么。

abstract.en: See a line drawn from an effect back to its cause.
abstract.cn: 想象一条线从结果往回连到原因。

abstract.en: See a signature appear under a painting that had none.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅原本无款的画作下方浮现出签名。

examples.en: Kindness was his most striking attribute.
examples.cn: 善良是他最突出的特质。

examples.en: She attributes her success to hard work.
examples.cn: 她把自己的成功归功于努力。

examples.en: The painting was attributed to an unknown artist.
examples.cn: 这幅画被认定出自一位不知名的画家之手。

dict_mnemonic.text: at-（向）加 tribute（分配）：分给某物的性质就是属性；把结果分回给某个原因，就是归因。

root: 源自拉丁语 attribuere「分派给」，由 ad-「向」与 tribuere「分配」构成，名词形式 attributum；经法语 attribut 进入英语，由「分派之物」引申为属性，又引申为把结果归到某个原因或作者名下。

sensesIntro.en: The same act of allotting produces both a quality and an explanation.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「分配」的动作，既产生了一种性质，也产生了一种解释。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label tied to a thing, naming its owner and nature.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张系在物品上的标签，写着它的归属与性质。

branches.en: attribute a painting to an artist

intro.en: The root tribute, 'to allot', links attribute with contribute and distribute.
intro.cn: 词根 tribute 意为「分配」，把 attribute 与 contribute、distribute 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin tribuere, 'to allot', also gives tribute and contribution.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 tribuere「分配」也是 tribute 与 contribution 的来源。

the act of naming a cause or author

definition_zh: 观众，听众；受众；正式会见
definition_en: the group of people who watch or listen to a performance, the people a work is aimed at, or a formal meeting with an important person
core_image: 剧场里暗下来，一束光打在台上，台下是一片安静的脸
scene: 演出开始前，主持人请全场把手机调成静音。The audience fell silent as the curtain rose.
sceneCN: 这里 audience 是「观众、听众」（第 1 个义项）；句意是大幕升起时，全场观众安静下来。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：面向受众的；易懂的

senses.title: People watching a show
senses.definition: the group of people who gather to watch or listen to a performance
senses.definitionCN: 聚集起来观看或聆听表演的一群人
senses.example: The audience fell silent as the curtain rose.
senses.exampleCN: 大幕升起时，全场观众安静下来。
senses.why: The Latin base audire means 'to hear', so the word began as a group of listeners and later took in people who watch as well.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 audire 意为「听」，所以这个词最初指一群听的人，后来也把看的人包括进来。

senses.title: People a work aims at
senses.definition: the particular group of people that a book, programme or product is meant for
senses.definitionCN: 某本书、节目或产品特意面向的那群人
senses.example: The magazine knows its audience well.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志很了解自己的读者群。
senses.why: Here nobody is physically present: the audience is imagined by the maker, a target group rather than a crowd in seats.
senses.whyCN: 这里的受众并不在场：它由创作者想象出来，是目标群体，而不是坐在座位上的那群人。

senses.title: Formal meeting
senses.definition: a formal meeting with a very important person
senses.definitionCN: 与极重要人物的正式会面
senses.example: The ambassador was granted an audience with the king.
senses.exampleCN: 大使获准觐见国王。
senses.why: The oldest court sense survives in this phrase: being admitted to be heard by a ruler, which is why the preposition is with.
senses.whyCN: 宫廷里的古老用法在这个短语里保留下来：获准让君主听你说话，所以介词用 with。

intro.en: Audience began as a word about hearing, not seeing.
intro.cn: audience 最初是个关于「听」而不是「看」的词。

items.en: audire meant 'to hear'.
items.cn: audire 意为「听见」。

items.en: audientia meant 'a hearing or attention'.
items.cn: audientia 意为「聆听、倾听」。

items.en: audience meant a hearing before a ruler.
items.cn: 古法语 audience 指在君主面前的听政会见。

items.en: English extended it to any group that listens.
items.cn: 英语把它扩展到任何一群聆听的人。

items.en: It now covers viewers, readers and target groups.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖观众、读者与目标受众。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aud- root of hearing; the near-meaning group gives words for people who watch or listen.
note.cn: 形近组共享表示「听」的 aud- 词根；近义组是表示观看者与聆听者的词。

entries.definition: a trial performance for a role

normalIntro.en: An audience is first a group that hears, then a group that watches, then a group a work is aimed at.
normalIntro.cn: audience 先是听的一群人，再是看的一群人，最后是作品瞄准的那群人。

normal.en: The root aud- means hear, as in audio and audible.
normal.cn: 词根 aud- 意为「听」，如 audio 与 audible。

normal.en: Audience is a collective noun: one audience, many audiences.
normal.cn: audience 是集合名词：一个观众群体，多个观众群体。

normal.en: Target audience is the phrase used in marketing and publishing.
normal.cn: target audience 是营销与出版里常用的说法。

normal.en: An audience with a king is a formal meeting, not a crowd.
normal.cn: an audience with a king 指正式会见，不是一群人。

normal.en: The verb form would be listen, not audience.
normal.cn: 表示动作时用 listen，不用 audience。

abstract.en: See a dark theatre with rows of still faces.
abstract.cn: 想象一间暗下来的剧场，一排排安静的脸。

abstract.en: See a single beam of light on a microphone.
abstract.cn: 想象一束光落在麦克风上。

abstract.en: See a magazine lying open with a note about its readers.
abstract.cn: 想象一本摊开的杂志，页边写着关于读者的备注。

examples.en: The audience fell silent as the curtain rose.
examples.cn: 大幕升起时，全场观众安静下来。

examples.en: The magazine knows its audience well.
examples.cn: 这本杂志很了解自己的读者群。

examples.en: The ambassador was granted an audience with the king.
examples.cn: 大使获准觐见国王。

dict_mnemonic.text: audi（听）加 -ence（名词）：听你说话的一群人是听众，看你表演的一群人是观众；作品心里瞄准的那群人是受众。

root: 源自拉丁语 audientia「聆听」，来自 audire「听见」；经古法语 audience 进入英语，最初指在君主面前获准陈说的正式会见，后来泛指听众与观众，现代又引申为作品面向的受众。

sensesIntro.en: A crowd in seats, an imagined readership and a royal appointment all count as an audience.
sensesIntro.cn: 坐在座位上的观众、想象中的读者群、宫廷里的觐见，都算 audience。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark hall of faces turned toward one lit stage.
core.cn: 核心意象：昏暗大厅里一张张脸朝向亮着的舞台。

intro.en: The root aud-, 'to hear', links audience with audio and audition.
intro.cn: 词根 aud- 意为「听」，把 audience 与 audio、audition 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, 'to hear', also gives audible and auditorium.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听见」也是 audible 与 auditorium 的来源。

items.meaning: a group that hears or watches

definition_zh: 声音的，音频的；音频，声音信号
definition_en: relating to sound that is recorded or broadcast, or the recorded sound itself
core_image: 一排跳动的波形，把看不见的声音画成看得见的线
scene: 剪辑师把画面定住，先单独处理声音那条轨道。The audio was clearer than the video.
sceneCN: 这里 audio 是「音频、声音信号」（第 2 个义项）；句意是音频比画面清楚。

senses.title: Relating to sound
senses.definition: connected with sound that is recorded, played back or broadcast
senses.definitionCN: 与录制、播放或播出的声音有关的
senses.example: The audio cable was loose at the back.
senses.exampleCN: 音频线在后面松了。
senses.why: As an adjective it simply labels the sound side of any system, standing opposite video in the same sentence.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，它只是给任何系统里「声音那一侧」贴标签，在同一句里与 video 相对。

senses.title: The sound itself
senses.definition: the recorded or transmitted sound itself
senses.definitionCN: 被录制或传输的声音本身
senses.example: The audio was clearer than the video.
senses.exampleCN: 音频比画面清楚。
senses.why: As a noun it turns the adjective into a mass of data: not a sound in the air, but a signal stored in a file.
senses.whyCN: 作名词时，形容词变成了可供处理的一团数据：不是空气里的声音，而是存在文件里的信号。

intro.en: Audio is simply the Latin word for 'I hear', taken whole into modern technology.
intro.cn: audio 就是拉丁语「我听见」，被整体搬进了现代技术。

items.en: audire meant 'to hear'.
items.cn: audire 意为「听见」。

items.en: audio was the first person form, 'I hear'.
items.cn: audio 是第一人称形式，意为「我听见」。

items.en: The root aud- was used to name hearing and sound.
items.cn: 词根 aud- 被用来命名听觉与声音。

items.en: audio labeled the sound channel beside video.
items.cn: 录音时代用 audio 标注与视频并列的声音通道。

items.en: It now covers files, streams and equipment.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖文件、流媒体与设备。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the aud- root; the near-meaning group gives other words for sound.
note.cn: 形近组共享 aud- 词根；近义组是其他表示声音的词。

entries.definition: relating to sound in a space

normalIntro.en: Audio marks the sound half of any media system.
normalIntro.cn: audio 标注的是任何媒体系统里「声音的那一半」。

normal.en: The root aud- means hear, the same one in audience.
normal.cn: 词根 aud- 意为「听」，与 audience 同源。

normal.en: Audio is the everyday partner of video.
normal.cn: audio 是 video 最日常的搭档。

normal.en: It stays the same in the plural, and usually takes no article as a noun.
normal.cn: 它复数形式不变，作名词时通常不加冠词。

normal.en: An audio file is a file that holds sound.
normal.cn: audio file 就是存放声音的文件。

normal.en: Audiobook simply joins audio and book.
normal.cn: audiobook 就是把 audio 与 book 拼在一起。

abstract.en: See a waveform rising and falling on a screen.
abstract.cn: 想象屏幕上一条上下起伏的波形。

abstract.en: See two cables, one for sound and one for picture.
abstract.cn: 想象两根线，一根走声音，一根走画面。

abstract.en: See a pair of headphones resting on a script.
abstract.cn: 想象一副耳机搁在剧本上。

examples.en: The audio was clearer than the video.
examples.cn: 音频比画面清楚。

examples.en: The audio cable was loose at the back.
examples.cn: 音频线在后面松了。

examples.en: She listened to the audio while reading the notes.
examples.cn: 她一边看笔记一边听录音。

dict_mnemonic.text: audi（听）加 -o：凡是被听见、被录下来的声音都归它管，所以音频文件、音频线、音质都用 audio。

root: 直接借自拉丁语 audio「我听见」，词根 audire 意为「听」；二十世纪录音与广播技术把它固定为「声音信号」的标签，与 video 相对。

sensesIntro.en: The same word labels the sound channel and the sound data inside it.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个词既标注声音通道，也指通道里流动的声音数据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a waveform drawn as a line of hills and valleys.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条画成山峰与山谷的波形线。

intro.en: The root aud-, 'to hear', runs through audio, audience and audition.
intro.cn: 词根 aud- 意为「听」，贯穿 audio、audience 与 audition。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, 'to hear', also gives audible and inaudible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听见」也是 audible 与 inaudible 的来源。

items.meaning: a hearing to test a performer

definition_zh: 姑母；姨母；伯母；婶母；舅母；阿姨
definition_en: the sister of your father or mother, or the wife of your uncle, or a polite name for an older woman
core_image: 过年时门口站着的那位长辈，手里提着给孩子的点心
scene: 孩子放暑假第一站就去了亲戚家，进门先喊人。My aunt lives near the sea.
sceneCN: 这里 aunt 是「姑母、姨母一类的长辈女性」（第 1 个义项）；句意是我姑妈住在海边。

pos.zh: 名词：姑母；姨母；伯母；婶母；舅母；阿姨

collocations.zh: 姑妈和姑父（泛指叔伯长辈）

senses.title: Parent's sister
senses.titleCN: 姑母；姨母；伯母；婶母；舅母
senses.definition: the sister of your father or mother, or the wife of your uncle
senses.definitionCN: 父亲或母亲的姐妹，也可以是叔伯舅父的妻子
senses.example: My aunt lives near the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 我姑妈住在海边。
senses.why: English has one word where Chinese splits the role by side and by marriage, so aunt covers several exact family positions at once.
senses.whyCN: 英语用一个词覆盖中文按父系母系、血缘婚姻分出的好几种称谓，所以 aunt 同时指多个精确的亲属位置。

senses.title: Friendly name for an older woman
senses.titleCN: 阿姨（对年长女性的称呼）
senses.definition: a polite or friendly way for a child to address an older woman
senses.definitionCN: 孩子对年长女性礼貌而亲切的称呼
senses.example: Aunt Li gave the children sweets.
senses.exampleCN: 李阿姨给孩子们发了糖。
senses.why: The kinship word is borrowed outside the family as a warm form of address, common in many cultures and very common in Chinese English.
senses.whyCN: 这个亲属词被借到家庭之外，变成一种亲切的称呼，在许多文化里都常见，在中文语境下的英语里尤其普遍。

intro.en: Aunt came into English from French, but its deepest root is Latin for a father's sister.
intro.cn: aunt 经法语进入英语，更深的词源是拉丁语里「父亲的姐妹」。

items.en: amita meant 'father's sister'.
items.cn: amita 意为「父亲的姐妹」。

items.en: ante was the everyday word for an aunt.
items.cn: 古法语 ante 是「姑母、姨母」的日常说法。

items.en: aunte covered both sides of the family.
items.cn: 中古英语 aunte 已兼指父系与母系。

items.en: The spelling settled as aunt while the sound stayed short.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 aunt，读音却保持短促。

items.en: The word also became a friendly title for older women.
items.cn: 这个词也成为对年长女性的亲切称呼。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that sound almost the same; the near-meaning group holds kinship words.
note.cn: 形近组是读音几乎相同的词；近义组是亲属称谓。

normalIntro.en: One short word covers every aunt on both sides of the family.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词覆盖了父系母系所有女性长辈。

normal.en: British English rhymes it with aren't; American English rhymes it with ant.
normal.cn: 英式读音与 aren't 押韵，美式读音与 ant 押韵。

normal.en: Add -ie or -y for a warmer, more childish auntie or aunty.
normal.cn: 加上 -ie 或 -y 就变成更亲昵、更孩子气的 auntie 或 aunty。

normal.en: Great-aunt moves one generation up from your aunt.
normal.cn: great-aunt 比 aunt 再高一辈。

normal.en: English does not say father's aunt for a grandparent's sister; it says great-aunt.
normal.cn: 英语不用「父亲的姑母」这种说法，而用 great-aunt。

normal.en: Aunt can stand alone as a title before a name.
normal.cn: aunt 可以单独放在名字前作称呼。

abstract.en: See a doorway with a paper bag of fruit in one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象门口站着一个人，手里提着一袋水果。

abstract.en: See a child pulled into a warm hug at the door.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子在门口被拉进一个温暖的拥抱。

abstract.en: See a family photo with one face circled in pencil.
abstract.cn: 想象一张全家福，其中一张脸被铅笔圈出来。

examples.en: My aunt lives near the sea.
examples.cn: 我姑妈住在海边。

examples.en: Aunt Li gave the children sweets.
examples.cn: 李阿姨给孩子们发了糖。

examples.en: We stayed with my aunt for a week.
examples.cn: 我们在姑妈家住了一个星期。

dict_mnemonic.text: 英语不区分父系母系，一个 aunt 就把姑母、姨母、伯母、婶母、舅母全包了；对邻家年长女性也能叫 aunt。

root: 源自拉丁语 amita「父亲的姐妹」，经古法语 ante 进入中古英语作 aunte；英语不再区分父系母系，于是这个词兼指姑母、姨母与叔伯舅父的妻子，后来又扩展为对年长女性的亲切称呼。

sensesIntro.en: The same short word names a real relative and a warmly addressed neighbour.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个短词，既称呼真正的亲属，也称呼亲切招呼的邻家长辈。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a familiar older woman at the door with a gift.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位熟悉的长辈女性站在门口，手里拿着礼物。

branches.en: my aunt on my mother's side

intro.en: Aunt itself takes no prefix, but -ie and -y build the warm forms auntie and aunty.
intro.cn: aunt 本身不加前缀，但 -ie 与 -y 构成亲昵形式 auntie 与 aunty。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root amita survives only in learned words, not in everyday English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根 amita 只残留在书面词里，日常英语已不再使用。

items.meaning: the child of an aunt or uncle

definition_zh: 作者，作家；发起者，创始人；撰写，创作
definition_en: a person who writes a book or other work, the person who started a plan or idea, or to write something
core_image: 书页最上方印着一个人的名字，下面才是正文
scene: 新书发布会上，主持人请写这本书的人先讲两句。The author signed copies for two hours.
sceneCN: 这里 author 是「作者、作家」（第 1 个义项）；句意是作者签了两个小时的书。

senses.title: Writer of a work
senses.definition: a person who writes a book, article or other text
senses.definitionCN: 写书、写文章或其他文字作品的人
senses.example: The author signed copies for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 作者签了两个小时的书。
senses.why: The Latin source auctor meant an originator, so the writer is seen as the person from whom the text comes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 auctor 意为「开创者」，所以作者被视为文本从之而来的那个人。

senses.title: Person who started something
senses.definition: the person who first thought of or started a plan, idea or change
senses.definitionCN: 最先想到或发起某个计划、想法、变革的人
senses.example: She is the author of the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 她是这场改革的发起者。
senses.why: The word keeps its older sense of originator: nothing needs to be written down for someone to be the author of a plan.
senses.whyCN: 这个词保留了「开创者」的旧义：要成为一项计划的发起者，并不需要真的写下什么。

senses.title: Write something
senses.definition: to write a book, report or other work yourself
senses.definitionCN: 亲自写出书、报告或其他作品
senses.example: He authored three reports on the case.
senses.exampleCN: 他就这个案子撰写了三份报告。
senses.why: The verb is modern and slightly formal; it stresses who produced the text rather than the act of writing itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词用法较新且偏正式，强调的是文本由谁产出，而不是书写这个动作本身。

intro.en: Author and authority grow from the same Latin word for an originator.
intro.cn: author 与 authority 出自同一个表示「开创者」的拉丁词。

items.en: augere meant 'to increase or make grow'.
items.cn: augere 意为「增加、使生长」。

items.en: auctor meant 'originator, promoter or seller'.
items.cn: auctor 意为「开创者、推动者、让与者」。

items.en: autor named the writer of a work.
items.cn: 古法语 autor 指作品的写作者。

items.en: English author covered both writer and founder.
items.cn: 中古英语 author 兼指写作者与创立者。

items.en: A verb use appeared, meaning to write a work.
items.cn: 现代英语又出现动词用法，意为撰写作品。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auctor root; the near-meaning group gives words for writers and creators.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auctor 词根；近义组是表示写作者与创造者的词。

entries.definition: a person who makes something new
the person who starts an idea

normalIntro.en: An author is where a text or a plan begins.
normalIntro.cn: author 就是文本或计划的起点。

normal.en: The root auctor means originator, which is why a plan can have an author.
normal.cn: 词根 auctor 意为开创者，所以一项计划也能有 author。

normal.en: The noun is common; the verb is formal and usually about reports or books.
normal.cn: 名词很常见；动词偏正式，多用于报告或书。

normal.en: Authority is not a person but the power an author figure holds.
normal.cn: authority 不是人，而是作者式人物握有的权力。

normal.en: Co-author adds co- for a shared writer.
normal.cn: co-author 加 co- 表示共同写作的人。

normal.en: Authorship names the fact of being the author.
normal.cn: authorship 指作者身份这件事。

abstract.en: See a name printed above the title on a first page.
abstract.cn: 想象扉页上书名上方印着一个名字。

abstract.en: See a hand writing the last line and putting down the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手写完最后一行，把笔放下。

abstract.en: See a blueprint with one signature in the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一张蓝图，角落里有一个人签名。

examples.en: The author signed copies for two hours.
examples.cn: 作者签了两个小时的书。

examples.en: She is the author of the reform.
examples.cn: 她是这场改革的发起者。

examples.en: He authored three reports on the case.
examples.cn: 他就这个案子撰写了三份报告。

dict_mnemonic.text: author 与 authority 同源：开创者写下作品是作者，开创者握有的分量是权威；把计划想出来的人，也是计划的 author。

root: 源自拉丁语 auctor「开创者、推动者」，来自 augere「使生长」；经古法语 autor 进入英语，先指作品的写作者与事物的创立者，现代又发展出「撰写」的动词用法。

sensesIntro.en: A book, a reform and a report can each have someone who began them.
sensesIntro.cn: 一本书、一场改革、一份报告，都可以有一个开创它的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a name printed above the title, marking where the work begins.
core.cn: 核心意象：书名上方印着的名字，标出作品的起点。

intro.en: The root auctor, 'originator', links author with authority and authorize.
intro.cn: 词根 auctor 意为「开创者」，把 author 与 authority、authorize 连在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin augere, 'to increase', also lies behind auction and augment.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 augere「增加」也是 auction 与 augment 的来源。

items.meaning: the writer or starter of a work
the state of being the author

definition_zh: 权力，职权；当局，官方机构；权威，专家；权威性
definition_en: the power to give orders, an official body that has such power, a person whose knowledge is trusted, or the quality of being reliable
core_image: 一枚印章压在文件上，纸面立刻有了分量
scene: 小区要修路，居民先去找能拍板的那一方。The local authority approved the plan.
sceneCN: 这里 authority 是「当局、官方机构」（第 2 个义项）；句意是地方当局批准了这项计划。

senses.title: Power to give orders
senses.definition: the right or power to give orders and make decisions
senses.definitionCN: 下命令、作决定的资格或力量
senses.example: The manager has the authority to hire staff.
senses.exampleCN: 这位经理有权雇用员工。
senses.why: The Latin source auctor meant an originator, and the derived noun named the weight an originator carries, so authority is power that comes from standing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源 auctor 意为开创者，派生名词指开创者身上的分量，所以 authority 是由地位带来的权力。

senses.title: Official body
senses.definition: an official organization or government body with power in an area
senses.definitionCN: 在某领域拥有权力的官方组织或政府机构
senses.example: The local authority approved the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 地方当局批准了这项计划。
senses.why: Power is transferred from a person to an institution, so the plural authorities often means the people who run a city or a service.
senses.whyCN: 权力从个人转到机构身上，所以复数 authorities 常指管理一座城市或某项公共事务的部门。

senses.title: Trusted expert
senses.definition: a person whose knowledge or judgment is respected and trusted
senses.definitionCN: 知识或判断受人尊重与信任的人
senses.example: She is an authority on ancient coins.
senses.exampleCN: 她是古钱币方面的权威。
senses.why: Here the weight is intellectual rather than official: the person is trusted because of knowledge, not because of an office.
senses.whyCN: 这里的分量是知识上的而非官职上的：此人受信任靠的是学问，而不是职位。

intro.en: Authority names the weight that an originator carries.

senses.title: Car, short form

senses.title: Machine works alone
senses.definition: working by itself without a person operating it
senses.definitionCN: 不需要人操作就能自己运转的
senses.example: The doors are automatic, so you need not touch them.
senses.exampleCN: 这些门是自动的，不用手碰。
senses.why: Greek automatos described something acting of its own will, and machines took over that sense: the mechanism plays the role of the will.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 automatos 描述「按自己的意愿行动」，机器接过了这层意思：机械装置扮演了意愿的角色。

senses.title: Done without thinking
senses.definition: done as a habit or reflex, without conscious thought
senses.definitionCN: 作为习惯或本能做出，不经思考的
senses.example: Answering the phone is automatic for her.
senses.exampleCN: 接电话对她来说是不假思索的事。
senses.why: A person can also run on autopilot: the body acts by itself, so the machine word is applied to human habit.
senses.whyCN: 人也能靠「自动驾驶」运转：身体自己动起来，于是这个机器词被用到人的习惯上。

senses.title: Certain to follow
senses.definition: certain to happen as a natural result of something
senses.definitionCN: 作为某事的自然结果必然发生的
senses.example: A price cut means an automatic rise in sales.
senses.exampleCN: 降价必然带来销量上升。
senses.why: If a result follows a cause with no choice involved, it is automatic in the logical sense, like a machine that cannot do otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 如果结果毫无选择地跟着原因出现，它在逻辑意义上就是自动的，像一台不可能有别的动作的机器。

normal.en: Automatic doors and automatic updates are the most common modern uses.

normal.en: An automatic response is a reflex, not a decision.

normal.en: The adverb adds -ally: automatically.

normal.en: Do not confuse it with automated, which describes a process converted to machines.

senses.title: By machine, unaided

items.en: mobile came from Latin mobilis, 'able to move'.
items.cn: mobile 来自拉丁语 mobilis，意为「能移动的」。

items.en: automobile was coined for a self-moving vehicle.
items.cn: automobile 被造出来指自行移动的车辆。

items.en: English adopted it as the formal word for a motor car.
items.cn: 英语在 1897 年采用它作为汽车的正式说法。

items.en: Everyday speech shortened it to auto and car.
items.cn: 日常口语把它缩短成 auto 与 car。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auto- prefix; the near-meaning group gives words for road vehicles.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auto- 前缀；近义组是表示道路车辆的词。

entries.definition: a road vehicle for a few passengers
a car, in older British use

normalIntro.en: Automobile is a description turned into a name: self plus moving.
normalIntro.cn: automobile 是把一个描述变成了名字：自己加移动。

normal.en: Break it into auto, self, and mobile, moving.
normal.cn: 拆成 auto「自己」和 mobile「可移动的」。

normal.en: It is the formal word; car is the everyday one.
normal.cn: 它是正式说法，car 是日常说法。

normal.en: Before another noun it keeps the singular: automobile industry.
normal.cn: 放在另一名词前时用单数：automobile industry。

normal.en: The short form auto belongs to American English.
normal.cn: 缩略形式 auto 属于美式英语。

normal.en: Automotive is the adjective used for the whole industry.
normal.cn: automotive 是用于整个行业的形容词。

abstract.en: See a carriage roll forward with no horse in front.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆马车向前走，前面却没有马。

abstract.en: See a factory line of identical bodies in a row.
abstract.cn: 想象工厂流水线上一排一模一样的车身。

abstract.en: See an old photo of a street half horse, half engine.
abstract.cn: 想象一张老照片，街上半是马车，半是汽车。

examples.en: The automobile changed how cities grew.
examples.cn: 汽车改变了城市扩张的方式。

examples.en: He works in the automobile industry.
examples.cn: 他在汽车行业工作。

examples.en: The museum keeps an early automobile in working order.
examples.cn: 博物馆保存着一辆仍能开动的早期汽车。

dict_mnemonic.text: auto（自己）加 mobile（能动的）：不用马拉、自己会走的车，就是 automobile；放到名词前就表示「汽车的」。

root: 由希腊语 autos「自己」与拉丁语 mobilis「能移动的」组合，经法语 automobile 进入英语；十九世纪末用来命名不用马拉的机动车，后来日常口语简化为 auto 与 car。

sensesIntro.en: The name describes the machine, and the same word can label the whole industry.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个名字描述机器本身，同一个词也能标注整个行业。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carriage that moves with no horse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆不用马拉却自己在走的马车。

intro.en: The prefix auto-, 'self', joins mobile, 'moving', to make automobile.
intro.cn: 前缀 auto-「自己」加 mobile「可移动的」，构成 automobile。

latinIntro.en: The moving half is Latin mobilis; the self half is Greek autos.
latinIntro.cn: 「移动」那一半来自拉丁语 mobilis，「自己」那一半来自希腊语 autos。

definition_zh: 秋天，秋季；（人生的）成熟期，暮年
definition_en: the season between summer and winter, or the later, maturing part of life
core_image: 树叶一夜之间转黄，风一吹就落了一层
scene: 开学那天风变凉了，校门口的梧桐开始掉叶子。The leaves turn gold in autumn.
sceneCN: 这里 autumn 是「秋天」（第 1 个义项：夏冬之间的季节）；句意是秋天树叶变成金黄色。

derivatives.zh: 形容词：秋天的；成熟期的
副词：如秋地；带着秋意地

senses.title: Season after summer
senses.definition: the season between summer and winter, when leaves fall and crops are gathered
senses.definitionCN: 夏冬之间的季节，树叶飘落、庄稼收获
senses.example: The leaves turn gold in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 秋天树叶变成金黄色。
senses.why: The word came through French from Latin autumnus, the name of the harvest season, so its core is the time of gathering rather than of cold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语 autumnus，本是收获季节的名字，所以它的核心是收成之时，而不是寒冷之时。

senses.title: Later part of life
senses.definition: the later part of a person's life, when experience has ripened
senses.definitionCN: 人生较后的阶段，经验已经成熟
senses.example: He wrote his best poems in the autumn of life.
senses.exampleCN: 他在人生的暮年写出了最好的诗。
senses.why: Because autumn is the season of ripening and slow decline, writers use it for the mature years before winter, which stands for old age and death.
senses.whyCN: 秋天是成熟与缓缓衰落的季节，所以文人用它指冬季之前的成熟岁月，而冬季象征老年与死亡。

intro.en: Autumn began as the name of the harvest season.
intro.cn: autumn 最初是收获季节的名字。

items.en: autumnus named the season of ripening and harvest.
items.cn: autumnus 指成熟与收获的季节。

items.en: automne carried the word into French.
items.cn: 古法语 automne 承接了这个词。

items.en: English borrowed it beside the native word harvest.
items.cn: 英语借入这个词，与本土词 harvest 并存。

items.en: Autumn took over as the season name in Britain.
items.cn: 在英国，autumn 逐渐取代 harvest 成为季节名。

items.en: American English kept fall, while autumn stayed literary in both.
items.cn: 美式英语保留 fall，而 autumn 在两种英语里都偏书面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words with a similar ending; the near-meaning group gives season words.
note.cn: 形近组是词尾相近的词；近义组是季节相关的词。

entries.definition: one of the four parts of the year

normalIntro.en: Autumn is the harvest season, and by metaphor the harvest years of a life.
normalIntro.cn: autumn 是收获的季节，比喻义上就是人生的收获之年。

normal.en: The n at the end is silent: autumn sounds like aw-tum.
normal.cn: 词尾的 n 不发音，读起来像 aw-tum。

normal.en: British English prefers autumn; American English often says fall.
normal.cn: 英式英语多用 autumn，美式英语常说 fall。

normal.en: In autumn takes the preposition in, not on.
normal.cn: 表示在秋天用介词 in，不用 on。

normal.en: The adjective is autumnal, with the stress moved forward.
normal.cn: 形容词是 autumnal，重音前移。

normal.en: The autumn of life means old age, not a date.
normal.cn: the autumn of life 指暮年，不是某个日期。

abstract.en: See a pavement covered with yellow leaves after wind.
abstract.cn: 想象起风后人行道上铺满黄叶。

abstract.en: See a field already cut and tied into bundles.
abstract.cn: 想象田里已经收割，捆成一束束。

abstract.en: See a grey head bent over a page by a window.
abstract.cn: 想象一位灰白头发的老人俯身在窗边读页。

examples.en: The leaves turn gold in autumn.
examples.cn: 秋天树叶变成金黄色。

examples.en: He wrote his best poems in the autumn of life.
examples.cn: 他在人生的暮年写出了最好的诗。

examples.en: The autumn term begins in September.
examples.cn: 秋季学期九月开始。

dict_mnemonic.text: autumn 本是「收获季」：叶子黄了、庄稼收了，就是秋天；人生收成的时候，也就是暮年。

root: 源自拉丁语 autumnus「成熟与收获的季节」，经古法语 automne 进入中古英语；在英国逐渐取代本土词 harvest 成为季节名，又由收获之意引申出「人生成熟期、暮年」的比喻义。

sensesIntro.en: One season name covers both the turning leaves and the ripening years of a life.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个季节名，既指转黄的树叶，也指人生渐熟的岁月。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a layer of gold leaves on a cold pavement.
core.cn: 核心意象：冰凉人行道上铺着一层金黄落叶。

intro.en: Autumn takes the adjective ending -al to make autumnal.
intro.cn: autumn 加形容词词尾 -al 构成 autumnal。

latinIntro.en: Latin autumnus is also the source of the adjective autumnalis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 autumnus 也是形容词 autumnalis 的来源。

definition_zh: 辅助的，备用的；辅助人员；助动词
definition_en: giving extra help or support, a person or thing that helps, or a verb used with a main verb
core_image: 主发动机旁边还有一台小机器，随时准备接手
scene: 医院停电的那一秒，备用电源自己接了上来。The auxiliary generator started at once.
sceneCN: 这里 auxiliary 是「备用的、辅助的」（第 1 个义项：提供额外支持）；句意是备用发电机立刻启动了。

derivatives.zh: 名词：辅助人员；助动词（复数）

senses.title: Giving extra support
senses.definition: giving additional help or serving as a reserve
senses.definitionCN: 提供额外帮助或作为后备的
senses.example: The auxiliary generator started at once.
senses.exampleCN: 备用发电机立刻启动了。
senses.why: The Latin base auxilium means help, so the adjective marks whatever stands beside the main thing and helps when needed.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基 auxilium 意为「帮助」，所以这个形容词标记的是站在主体旁边、需要时出手帮忙的东西。

senses.title: Helper or support worker
senses.definition: a person or group that gives support to a main body
senses.definitionCN: 为主要机构提供支持的人或队伍
senses.example: The hospital hired more auxiliary staff.
senses.exampleCN: 医院雇用了更多辅助人员。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a countable noun for the people who provide the help, especially in hospitals, armies and offices.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成可数名词，指提供帮助的那些人，在医院、军队与机关里尤其常见。

senses.title: Helping verb
senses.definition: a verb such as be, have or will that helps form another verb's tense or voice
senses.definitionCN: be、have、will 这类帮助构成另一个动词时态或语态的动词
senses.example: In this sentence, will is an auxiliary.
senses.exampleCN: 在这个句子里，will 是助动词。
senses.why: Grammar borrowed the same idea: the helping verb carries tense or voice while the main verb carries the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 语法借用了同一个思路：助动词承担时态或语态，主要动词承担词义。

intro.en: Auxiliary comes from a Latin word for help.
intro.cn: auxiliary 来自拉丁语中表示「帮助」的词。

items.en: auxilium meant 'help or support'.
items.cn: auxilium 意为「帮助、支援」。

items.en: auxiliarius meant 'giving help'.
items.cn: auxiliarius 意为「提供帮助的」。

items.en: auxilia named supporting troops.
items.cn: auxilia 指辅助部队。

items.en: French auxiliaire carried both the adjective and the noun.
items.cn: 法语 auxiliaire 兼有形容词与名词用法。

items.en: English added the grammar sense of a helping verb.
items.cn: 英语又加上了「助动词」这一语法义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the auxili- stem; the near-meaning group gives words for support and reserve.
note.cn: 形近组共享 auxili- 词干；近义组是表示支持与后备的词。

entries.definition: less important than the main thing

normalIntro.en: Auxiliary marks whatever stands beside the main thing and helps.
normalIntro.cn: auxiliary 标记的是站在主体旁边帮忙的那一方。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable: awg-ZIL-yuh-ree.
normal.cn: 重音在第二音节：awg-ZIL-yuh-ree。

normal.en: Auxiliary verb is the phrase to remember for grammar.
normal.cn: 语法里要记住的是 auxiliary verb 这个说法。

normal.en: The plural is auxiliaries, and it often means support staff.
normal.cn: 复数是 auxiliaries，常指辅助人员。

normal.en: Auxiliary power is the electricity kept for emergencies.
normal.cn: auxiliary power 指为应急保留的电力。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with auxiliary's look-alike auxin, a plant hormone.
normal.cn: 不要与形近词 auxin 混淆，那是植物生长素。

abstract.en: See a small engine switch on beside a big one.
abstract.cn: 想象一台小发动机在大发动机旁边启动。

abstract.en: See a second key already in the lock.
abstract.cn: 想象第二把钥匙已经插在锁里。

abstract.en: See a helping hand steady a ladder from below.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从下面扶稳梯子。

examples.en: The auxiliary generator started at once.
examples.cn: 备用发电机立刻启动了。

examples.en: The hospital hired more auxiliary staff.
examples.cn: 医院雇用了更多辅助人员。

examples.en: In this sentence, will is an auxiliary.
examples.cn: 在这个句子里，will 是助动词。

dict_mnemonic.text: auxili 意为「帮助」，加 -ary：在旁边帮忙的设备是备用的，帮忙的人是辅助人员，帮忙构成时态的词是助动词。

root: 源自拉丁语 auxiliarius「提供帮助的」，来自 auxilium「帮助、支援」，auxilia 指辅助部队；经法语 auxiliaire 进入英语，由「帮忙的」引申为备用设备、辅助人员与语法上的助动词。

sensesIntro.en: Help can be a machine, a person or a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 帮助可以是一台机器、一个人，也可以是一个动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small engine waiting beside the main one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台小发动机在主发动机旁边待命。

intro.en: The stem auxili-, 'help', takes -ary to make auxiliary.
intro.cn: 词干 auxili- 意为「帮助」，加 -ary 构成 auxiliary。

latinIntro.en: Latin auxilium, 'help', gives the whole family its shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 auxilium「帮助」决定了整个词族的形态。

definition_zh: 可获得的，可用的；有空的；有效的（票、座位等仍可购买）
definition_en: able to be obtained or used, free to see someone, or still open to be bought
core_image: 货架上还留着一件，手伸过去就能拿到
scene: 订票页面刷新了一下，原本灰掉的座位重新亮起。Two seats are still available.
sceneCN: 这里 available 是「可获得的、可用的」（第 1 个义项：还能拿到）；句意是还有两个座位可选。

pos.zh: 形容词：可获得的；有空的；有效的

derivatives.zh: 形容词：不可获得的；没空的

senses.title: Able to be had
senses.definition: able to be obtained, bought or used
senses.definitionCN: 能够被取得、买到或使用的
senses.example: Two seats are still available.
senses.exampleCN: 还有两个座位可选。
senses.why: The word is built on avail, 'to be of use or worth', so available describes something that is there and can be put to use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 avail「有用、有价值」之上，所以 available 描述的是东西就在那里、可以拿来用。

senses.title: Free to meet
senses.definition: not busy, and therefore free to meet or talk
senses.definitionCN: 不忙，因此可以见面或交谈
senses.example: The doctor is available after three.
senses.exampleCN: 医生三点以后有空。
senses.why: A person, like a thing, can be on hand and ready to be used; here the use is someone's time rather than an object.
senses.whyCN: 人像物品一样，可以在手边、随时可用；只是这里的「用」指的是对方的时间，而不是物件。

senses.title: Still open to buy
senses.definition: not yet sold or booked, and therefore still open to customers
senses.definitionCN: 尚未售出或订走，因此仍向顾客开放
senses.example: The ticket is available until Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 这张票在周五之前都能买。
senses.why: In ticketing the word narrows to stock that has not been taken, which is why it so often appears beside seats and rooms.
senses.whyCN: 在售票语境里，这个词收窄为「还没被拿走的名额」，所以常与座位、房间一起出现。

intro.en: Available grows from an old verb meaning to be of worth or use.
intro.cn: available 来自一个古老动词，意为「有价值、有用处」。

items.en: valere meant 'to be strong or be worth'.
items.cn: valere 意为「有力量、有价值」。

items.en: valoir meant 'to be worth'.
items.cn: 古法语 valoir 意为「值、有用」。

items.en: availer meant 'to be of use or help'.
items.cn: 古法语 availer 意为「有用、有帮助」。

items.en: English avail kept the sense of being useful.
items.cn: 英语 avail 保留了「有用」的意思。

items.en: The adjective named what can be used or obtained.
items.cn: 形容词形式指可以被使用或取得的东西。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the avail root; the near-meaning group gives words for reachable things and free time.
note.cn: 形近组共享 avail 词根；近义组是表示可得之物与空闲时间的词。

normalIntro.en: Available says something or someone is there and can be used.
normalIntro.cn: available 表示某物或某人在那里、可以用得上。

normal.en: The base is avail, to be of use, plus -able, able to.
normal.cn: 词基是 avail「有用」，加 -able「能够」。

normal.en: Available to names who may use it; available for names the purpose.
normal.cn: available to 引出可以使用的人，available for 引出用途。

normal.en: For people it means not busy, as in the doctor is available.
normal.cn: 用于人时表示不忙，例如医生有空。

normal.en: Readily available means easy to get, not merely existing.
normal.cn: readily available 表示容易得到，不只是存在。

normal.en: Unavailable adds un- and means the opposite.
normal.cn: 加 un- 构成 unavailable，意思相反。

abstract.en: See one last item still sitting on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象货架上还剩下最后一件。

abstract.en: See a grey seat turn green on a booking screen.
abstract.cn: 想象订票屏幕上灰色座位变成绿色。

abstract.en: See an open door and a free chair in an office.
abstract.cn: 想象办公室门开着，椅子空着。

examples.en: Two seats are still available.
examples.cn: 还有两个座位可选。

examples.en: The doctor is available after three.
examples.cn: 医生三点以后有空。

examples.en: The ticket is available until Friday.
examples.cn: 这张票在周五之前都能买。

dict_mnemonic.text: avail（有用）加 -able（能够）：东西能拿到、能用上是可获得的，人的时间能用上是 有空的，票还没卖完是仍可购买的。

root: 源自中古英语 avail「有用、有价值」，更早来自古法语 availer 与拉丁语 valere「有力量、有价值」；加形容词词尾 -able 后表示「可以被取得或使用」，再由物及人，引申为「有空」。

sensesIntro.en: A product, a person's time and an unsold ticket can all be available.
sensesIntro.cn: 一件商品、一个人的时间、一张没卖出的票，都可以是 available。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one last item on the shelf within reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：货架上还剩一件，伸手可及。

intro.en: The root avail, 'to be of use', takes -able to make available.
intro.cn: 词根 avail 意为「有用」，加 -able 构成 available。

latinIntro.en: Latin valere, 'to be worth', also gives value, valid and evaluate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 valere「有价值」也是 value、valid 与 evaluate 的来源。

items.meaning: able to be used or had
